X→A  ..............  \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0B→Y  ....\n\t\t\t\t\t15211 text assumption\n\t\t\t\t15212 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15213 text Really difficult Sufficient Assumption questions usually work by having a correct answer that Rules Out Possible Objections or a correct answer that works in an unexpected way. \n\t\t\t\t\t15214 text Instead of finding an answer with the "perfect" missing link we were looking for, we might find a correct answer whose trigger is implied by the evidence but was not directly stated by the evidence.\n\t\t\t\t\t15215 text We might find a correct answer that helps us complete a "binary argument", meaning it has the flow of "If X is true, then we ultimately get to our conclusion. And if X is not true, then we still get to our conclusion."\n\t\t\t\t15216 image Oh, the Humanities! \n\t\t\t\t15217 heading Oh, the Humanities!, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15218 text Oh, the Humanities!\n\t\t\t\t15219 text Process\n\t\t\t\t15220 text 52 mins\n\t\t\t\t15221 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15222 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15223 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15224 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15225 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15226 text It\'s no accident that we invoked the famous quote from the fiery crash of the Hindenburg blimp. Each of these level 5 \n\t\t\t\t\t15227 text Humanities\n\t\t\t\t\t15228 text  passages brought down many students\' RC scores on tests 59 and 79.\n\t\t\t\t\t15229 text So buckle up for a challenge, mostly on the backend of trying to get all the questions correct. \n\t\t\t\t\t15230 text The most common frameworks for Humanities passages are \n\t\t\t\t\t15231 text Highlight Noteworthy\n\t\t\t\t\t15232 text  (a descriptive essay emphasizing the essence, motivation, or importance of an artist\'s style) and \n\t\t\t\t\t15233 text Challenge Position\n\t\t\t\t\t15234 text  (an essay that defends an artist against criticism or clarifies a misconception people have about them).\n\t\t\t\t15235 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15236 text Try these two passages, \n\t\t\t\t\t15237 text untimed\n\t\t\t\t\t15238 text seeing if you can figure out all the correct answers\n\t\t\t\t\t15239 text In both passages, students often struggle to fully understand the aesthetic concerns or design properties of the artists being profiled, and some of the questions in these passage sets are just downright tricky.\n\t\t\t\t\t15240 text In order to get them all right, you\'ll probably have to select a few answers you don\'t really like, but you will be reassuring yourself, "This answer seems weird, ... but I guess I\'d have to say that this answer is the \n\t\t\t\t\t15241 text best available \n\t\t\t\t\t15242 text option". \n\t\t\t\t15243 image Agree / Disagree - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15244 heading Agree / Disagree - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15245 text Agree / Disagree - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15246 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15247 text 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15248 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15249 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15250 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15251 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15252 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15253 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct to conquer  \ufeffLevel 5 for \n\t\t\t\t\t15254 text Agree / Disagree\n\t\t\t\t\t15255 text .\n\t\t\t\t15256 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15257 text Remember that Disagree problems are usually like doing \n\t\t\t\t\t15258 text two \n\t\t\t\t\t15259 text Most Supported questions at once:\n\t\t\t\t\t15260 text The correct answer choice should be a claim we can pretty much derive from one of the two speakers. The negation of that answer choice should be a claim we can pretty much derive from the other speaker.\n\t\t\t\t\t15261 text One sneaky move we see a lot on harder Agree / Disagree problems involves arguing over a conditional claim. By using restrictive, conditional wording, a person is technically commenting on a lot of stuff they never directly referred to.\n\t\t\t\t\t15262 text For example, if Kenny says, "Only well-painted canvases should be considered art", then we know his opinion on all these claims, even though Kenny never mentioned \n\t\t\t\t\t15263 text bananas \n\t\t\t\t\t15264 text or \n\t\t\t\t\t15265 text Dr. Pepper\n\t\t\t\t\t15266 text : \n\t\t\t\t\t15267 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15268 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15269 text • Dressing up bananas as former presidents can be considered art.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15270 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15271 text • Smearing banana onto a glass picture frame can be considered art.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15272 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15273 text • Letting a banana slowly dissolve in a glass of Dr. Pepper can be considered art.\n\t\t\t\t\t15274 text We know that Kenny would disagree with all these claims, since his restrictive wording allows us to apply his standard of "\n\t\t\t\t\t15275 text only\n\t\t\t\t\t15276 text  well-painted canvases" to an infinite number of novel scenarios. \n\t\t\t\t15277 image Problem / Solution - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15278 heading Problem / Solution - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15279 text Problem / Solution - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15280 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15281 text 1 hr, 7 mins\n\t\t\t\t15282 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15283 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15284 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15285 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15286 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15287 text Synopsis\n\t\t\t\t\t15288 text This is the 3rd most common RC framework, showing in about 17% of passages, especially Law and Science passages. Usually these passages end with the author providing some recommendation or corrective, so just like \n\t\t\t\t\t15289 text Answer a Question \n\t\t\t\t\t15290 text and \n\t\t\t\t\t15291 text Present Debate \n\t\t\t\t\t15292 text and \n\t\t\t\t\t15293 text Old / New, \n\t\t\t\t\t15294 text we often don\'t hear the Author\'s voice or main point until the final paragraph.\n\t\t\t\t\t15295 text But in some cases, the author never provides a solution, and so our main point ends up sounding like a description of the Problem. \n\t\t\t\t\t15296 text Identifying Features\n\t\t\t\t\t15297 text One of the interesting parts of Problem / Solution passages is that we\'re very likely to get the \n\t\t\t\t\t15298 text Main Point \n\t\t\t\t\t15299 text in the\n\t\t\t\t\t15300 text  final paragraph\n\t\t\t\t\t15301 text , because the author tends to spend two or three paragraphs acquainting us with a problematic situation.\n\t\t\t\t\t15302 text Some passages only describe a Problem. This is typical in Law passages, where an author might want to explore a thorny legal issue that doesn\'t have any clear answers right now.\n\t\t\t\t\t15303 text Some Humanities passages will feel like the author is simply complaining about something, without offering a better way. Similarly, we could think of these critique passages as Presenting a Problem, but never offering a solution.\n\t\t\t\t\t15304 text Sometimes, the author will present or evaluate \n\t\t\t\t\t15305 text other people\'s \n\t\t\t\t\t15306 text proposed Solutions. If the author implicitly agrees with someone else\'s solution, then she\'ll usually put it towards the end and offer no pushback. In other passages, though, the author will shoot down other people\'s potential solutions before proposing her own (or giving up that there is still no good solution).\n\t\t\t\t15307 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15308 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct, \n\t\t\t\t\t15309 text to pass this Level.\n\t\t\t\t\t15310 text If it doesn\'t happen within 30 mins, that\'s fine. Feel free to keep working at it if you\'re so inclined, or to just come back to it at another time.\n\t\t\t\t\t15311 text As You\'re Reading ... \n\t\t\t\t\t15312 text \ufeffEarly Clues\n\t\t\t\t\t15313 text We are most likely to see hints of a problem in the first paragraph or usually by the first sentence of the 2nd paragraph at the latest. Words like "problematic", "the difficulty with this", "ambiguity", "uncertainty" and such suggest an air of tension.\n\t\t\t\t\t15314 text If we see an author pose a question or otherwise discuss smart people who have been trying to figure out how ____ , then answering that question is probably the central Problem the passage is focused on.\n\t\t\t\t\t15315 text Big Ideas to Track\n\t\t\t\t\t15316 text As you\'re reading these passages, look for language in the first paragraph or transition to the second that seems to be setting up something problematic or something negative.\n\t\t\t\t\t15317 text Start trying to fill in this blank: \n\t\t\t\t\t15318 text What is the \n\t\t\t\t\t15319 text Problem\n\t\t\t\t\t15320 text ? \n\t\t\t\t\t15321 text or otherwise, \n\t\t\t\t\t15322 text What \n\t\t\t\t\t15323 text Question \n\t\t\t\t\t15324 text are people trying to answer?\n\t\t\t\t\t15325 text As you learn more about it, keep reminding yourself of The Problem (or The Question). The other details don\'t matter, unless you can attach them to your strong, enduring memory of The Problem. Relate any details or new topics to the Problem.\n\t\t\t\t\t15326 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15327 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15328 text • Historical background  on the Problem?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15329 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15330 text • Causal explanation  for the Problem?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15331 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15332 text • Misconception  about the Problem?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15333 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15334 text • More  elaboration  on what the Problem is?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15335 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15336 text • Someone\'s opinion  about the Problem?\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15337 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15338 text • The  implications  if we don\'t solve this Problem?\n\t\t\t\t\t15339 text Will there be a Solution? Will there be a Recommendation? Omigosh, I\'m so excited, are you? I\'m obnoxiously overdramatizing to remind you to keep your ears open for hints that we\'re now pivoting into Solution territory. That\'s the other big idea we have to capture.\n\t\t\t\t\t15340 text If there\'s no Solution, then let\'s listen for a summary sentence towards the end in which the author wraps up the significance of the situation.\n\t\t\t\t15341 image Speedwalking LR (set 1)\n\t\t\t\t15342 heading Speedwalking LR (set 1), Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15343 text Speedwalking LR (set 1)\n\t\t\t\t15344 text Pacing\n\t\t\t\t15345 text 33 mins\n\t\t\t\t15346 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15347 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15348 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15349 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15350 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15351 text LENGTH\n\t\t\t\t\t15352 text  -- 15 Q\'s, 15 minutes (1.5x = 22, 2x = 30)\n\t\t\t\t\t15353 text TYPES\n\t\t\t\t\t15354 text  -- Paradox, Flaw, Role, Main Conclusion, Necessary Assumption, Sufficient Assumption, Strengthen, Weaken, Method, and Must Be True.\n\t\t\t\t\t15355 text LEVEL\n\t\t\t\t\t15356 text  -- 1\n\t\t\t\t\t15357 text Wait a sec -- these are all level 1? I thought this activity was listed as level 5?\n\t\t\t\t\t15358 text Yes, because the goal is something a level 5 student needs to work on:\xa0\xa0be able to quickly take care of easier questions, so that you\'ll have more time and brainpower in reserves for the harder, more flexible thinking questions in the section.\n\t\t\t\t\t15359 text \ufeffGiven how many subtle reading traps there are on LSAT, it\'s sometimes difficult to ever let yourself believe that an answer you find appealing is correct. "It\'s never this easy", we might think. But, sure it is! Sometimes it really is that easy. We need to improve our ability to \n\t\t\t\t\t15360 text let the easy be easy\n\t\t\t\t\t15361 text . \n\t\t\t\t\t15362 text And we need to develop enough self-trust while we\'re doing easier problems that we can pick up our pace when possible. \n\t\t\t\t15363 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15364 text Try to get through these 15 questions in 15 mins. Keep yourself going at a brisk pace. When you have a strong idea of what you\'re looking for (like on Main Conclusion, Role, Sufficient Assumption, Flaw), try to be proactive about scanning for and finding your answer, rather than reading all five choices start to finish.\n\t\t\t\t\t15365 text However, on tasks where we compare the impact of new information (like Paradox, Strengthen, Weaken), we may still need to use more time to consider all five answers.\n\t\t\t\t\t15366 text If your thinking feels unfinished on any of them, flag them as you go (so that you can maintain your brisk pace), and then take a second look at them after the timer goes off before you check your answer / the explanation.\n\t\t\t\t15367 image Science: Crop Crap\n\t\t\t\t15368 heading Science: Crop Crap, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15369 text Science: Crop Crap\n\t\t\t\t15370 text Pacing\n\t\t\t\t15371 text 33 mins\n\t\t\t\t15372 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15373 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15374 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15375 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15376 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15377 text As the inelegant name of this activity suggests, this is a pair of \n\t\t\t\t\t15378 text Science \n\t\t\t\t\t15379 text passages about  crops . \n\t\t\t\t\t15380 text You\'re welcome, you\'re welcome! Look, we had no choice. You guys have been blowing up our inbox requesting this. It feels good to finally deliver.\n\t\t\t\t\t15381 text You\'re doing this as a timed set.\xa0\xa0\n\t\t\t\t\t15382 text In other words, there\'s a small plot of land to harvest before the hurricane rolls in. You have 15-20 minutes. Grab the most get-able fruit while there\'s time! \n\t\t\t\t15383 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15384 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15385 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15386 text 1 . Set a timer for  18 minutes.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15387 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15388 text 2 . Attempt these two passages.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15389 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15390 text 3 . Select an answer to all 15 questions within the time limit, even if some of them are "flag-and-skip" answers.\n\t\t\t\t\t15391 text Once the timer goes off, and you go through answers / explanations, make sure you take 5 extra seconds as you\'re leaving each problem to mentally or vocally articulate a takeaway. Encode something in your subconscious: \n\t\t\t\t\t15392 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15393 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15394 text • something you did right\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15395 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15396 text • a question you wished you had asked yourself\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15397 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15398 text • a detail you wished you\'d noticed\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15399 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15400 text • a spot in the passage you wished you\'d researched\n\t\t\t\t15401 image Strengthen - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15402 heading Strengthen - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15403 text Strengthen - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15404 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15405 text 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15406 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15407 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15408 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15409 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15410 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15411 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct  to complete your \n\t\t\t\t\t15412 text Level\n\t\t\t\t\t15413 text  for \n\t\t\t\t\t15414 text level 5.\n\t\t\t\t15415 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15416 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15417 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15418 text • Set a timer for 20 minutes.\xa0If you haven\'t passed your level by the time the timer goes off, move on to something else or try another 10-15 mins if you want to keep pushing to clear the level.\n\t\t\t\t\t15419 text Try to articulate how your correct answer is helping the argument:\n\t\t\t\t\t15420 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15421 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15422 text • affirming  an  assumption ?\n\t\t\t\t\t15423 text (if the author was assuming "X is relevant to Y", a correct answer on strengthen might say something like "X is the most important factor for Y")\n\t\t\t\t\t15424 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15425 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15426 text • countering  a possible  objection  to the argument? \n\t\t\t\t\t15427 text (these answers are harder to interpret, if we didn\'t think of possible objections to the argument ahead of time. So even though this is \n\t\t\t\t\t15428 text Strengthen\n\t\t\t\t\t15429 text , don\'t neglect to figure out where the argument is vulnerable to criticism by considering objections, once you\'ve read the argument.\n\t\t\t\t\t15430 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15431 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15432 text • making the existing  evidence  seem  more compelling / relevant ?\n\t\t\t\t\t15433 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15434 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15435 text • adding  on some new consideration that gives \n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15436 text yet another reason\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15437 text  to believe the Conclusion?\n\t\t\t\t15438 image PrepTest 141 - Section 1\n\t\t\t\t15439 heading PrepTest 141 - Section 1, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15440 text PrepTest 141 - Section 1\n\t\t\t\t15441 text Timed Section 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15442 button Take Section\n\t\t\t\t\t15443 text Take Section\n\t\t\t\t15444 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15445 image PrepTest 142 - Section 4\n\t\t\t\t15446 heading PrepTest 142 - Section 4, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15447 text PrepTest 142 - Section 4\n\t\t\t\t15448 text Timed Section 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15449 button Take Section\n\t\t\t\t\t15450 text Take Section\n\t\t\t\t15451 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15452 image PrepTest 155\n\t\t\t\t15453 heading PrepTest 155, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15454 text PrepTest 155\n\t\t\t\t15455 text Practice Test 4 hrs, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15456 button Take Test\n\t\t\t\t\t15457 text Take Test\n\t\t\t\t15458 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15459 button \uf2c2\n\t\t\t\t\t15460 text \uf2c2\n\t\t\t15461 container\n\t\t\t\t15462 heading Week 14, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t15463 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15464 text Week  14\n\t\t\t\t15465 text December 27th, 2026 - January 2nd, 2027\n\t\t\t\t15466 text Est. Time Remaining:  22 hrs, 7 mins\n\t\t\t\t15467 text \uf113\n\t\t\t\t15468 image Science - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15469 heading Science - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15470 text Science - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15471 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15472 text 1 hr, 7 mins\n\t\t\t\t15473 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15474 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15475 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15476 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15477 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15478 heading Common Frameworks, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15479 text Common Frameworks\n\t\t\t\t\t15480 text The most common frameworks in Science passages are \n\t\t\t\t\t15481 text Old/New, Problem/Solution \n\t\t\t\t\t15482 text and \n\t\t\t\t\t15483 text Present a Debate\n\t\t\t\t\t15484 text . There is significant overlap here, as Old/New will frequently be applicable (there was an Old question we couldn\'t answer, but \n\t\t\t\t\t15485 text recent\n\t\t\t\t\t15486 text  findings suggest a New possible answer or solution, or there was a traditional school of thought and now there is a new school of thought coming at the same topic from a different point of view).\n\t\t\t\t15487 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15488 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct, \n\t\t\t\t\t15489 text to pass this Level.\n\t\t\t\t\t15490 text If it doesn\'t happen within 30 mins, that\'s fine. Feel free to keep working at it if you\'re so inclined, or to just come back to it at another time.\n\t\t\t\t\t15491 text As You\'re Reading\n\t\t\t\t\t15492 text If the details feel overwhelming, stop reading for a sec, and just remind yourself of the Big Ideas from your framework.\n\t\t\t\t\t15493 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15494 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15495 text • What is the question / problem  that scientists have been asking or trying to solve?\n\t\t\t\t\t15496 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15497 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15498 text • What is the answer / solution  to that question or problem?\n\t\t\t\t\t15499 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15500 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15501 text • This debate is about what  topic, mystery, phenomenon, or question?\n\t\t\t\t\t15502 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15503 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15504 text • What is the difference  between Point of View 1 and Point of View 2 (or 3 or 4). Define it in an oppositional "they believe X / they believe not-X" or "fast growth vs. slow growth" kind of way. Don\'t just say words associated with each side of the debate; make sure you frame them as logical opposites in some way.\n\t\t\t\t\t15505 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15506 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15507 text • Does the Author show up at the end  to let us know how she feels about this Debate or how she feels about this New answer/solution we\'re considering?\n\t\t\t\t\t15508 text Optional "Deluxe" Practice\n\t\t\t\t\t15509 text Pop open the NOTES panel (bottom left of the screen has a little page icon) and move/resize the NOTES window so that it covers the answers. Don\'t look at the answers until you\'ve \n\t\t\t\t\t15510 text written your prediction\n\t\t\t\t\t15511 text .\n\t\t\t\t\t15512 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15513 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15514 text • sometimes our prediction comes from our gut understanding\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15515 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15516 text • sometimes our prediction is simply "last sentence of paragraph 3"\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15517 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15518 text • sometimes you can\'t make a prediction (you can write "no prediction")\n\t\t\t\t\t15519 text When you ultimately see the correct answer, you can assess how well-aligned your prediction was / wasn\'t, and potentially learn more about that stage of the process.\n\t\t\t\t\t15520 text When you go to start looking at the answers, move the notes panel to the side and \n\t\t\t\t\t15521 text write in why you\'re rejecting each wrong answer\n\t\t\t\t\t15522 text . When you ultimately see the explanation, you can compare your reason to ours and see if there\'s anything to refine about your thinking there. \n\t\t\t\t15523 image Assumption Family (Harder) Set 2\n\t\t\t\t15524 heading Assumption Family (Harder) Set 2, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15525 text Assumption Family (Harder) Set 2\n\t\t\t\t15526 text Pacing\n\t\t\t\t15527 text 1 hr\n\t\t\t\t15528 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15529 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15530 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15531 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15532 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15533 text This is a \n\t\t\t\t\t15534 text tough \n\t\t\t\t\t15535 text timed set of Assumption Family problems from test 72, all level 4 or 5. 1 . Set a timer for  17 mins  (1.5x = 26, 2x = 34)\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15562 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15563 text 2 . Before timer runs out,  get an answer to all 10  problems, so that you can practice the tough habit of moving on even though you weren\'t fully done thinking about the problem.\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15564 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15565 text 3 . Once the timer goes off,  take an untimed 2nd look  at problems before you check your previous attempt and look at the explanation.\n\t\t\t\t\t15566 text Don\'t do this activity as your first LSAT activity of the day. It would be like not stretching at all and then just jumping into the 4th quarter of an NBA playoff game. Get your brain ready to have a really powerful stretch of high-processing efficiency for 20 mins. \n\t\t\t\t15567 image Principle-Strengthen - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15568 heading Principle-Strengthen - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15569 text Principle-Strengthen - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15570 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15571 text 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15572 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15573 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15574 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15575 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15576 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15577 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct\n\t\t\t\t\t15578 text , to pass this Level.\n\t\t\t\t\t15579 text question stem keywords\n\t\t\t\t\t15580 text principle, if valid / if assumed / if established, most justifies, most supports\n\t\t\t\t\t15581 text examples\n\t\t\t\t\t15582 text Which principle, if valid, most justifies the reasoning in the argument? Which principle, if established, most helps to justify the decision?\n\t\t\t\t15583 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15584 heading Principle-Strengthen, Value: 4\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15585 text Principle-Strengthen\n\t\t\t\t\t15586 heading   , Value: 4\n\t\t\t\t\t15587 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15588 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15589 text • Find the CONCLUSION and the EVIDENCE.\n\t\t\t\t\t15590 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15591 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15592 text • Pre-phrase "IF premise, THEN conclusion".\n\t\t\t\t\t15593 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15594 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15595 text • The correct answer should sound like 1/2 Premise language, 1/2 Conclusion language.\n\t\t\t\t\t15596 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15597 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15598 text • Try to get rid of answer choices quickly if they don\'t have Conclusion language\n\t\t\t\t\t15599 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15600 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15601 text • Also be wary of answers that put the Conclusion on the  left  side of arrow, or that say "not the Conclusion" on the  right  of the arrow.\n\t\t\t\t\t15602 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15603 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15604 text • If there are competing interests being weighted against each other, the correct answer may rank one thing as more important than another. We call this style of answer " weighing tradeoffs ".\n\t\t\t\t15605 image Society - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15606 heading Society - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15607 text Society - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15608 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15609 text 1 hr, 7 mins\n\t\t\t\t15610 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15611 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15612 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15613 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15614 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15615 heading Common Frameworks, Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15616 text Common Frameworks\n\t\t\t\t\t15617 text Society is harder to pin down. Topics in economics, sociology, and psychology tend to be more \n\t\t\t\t\t15618 text Challenge Position\n\t\t\t\t\t15619 text  (clarifying a misconception, usually) or \n\t\t\t\t\t15620 text Present Debate\n\t\t\t\t\t15621 text . Meanwhile, the passages that feel more like hard sciences about past cultures are more likely to have an \n\t\t\t\t\t15622 text Old / New \n\t\t\t\t\t15623 text or \n\t\t\t\t\t15624 text Problem / Solution \n\t\t\t\t\t15625 text vibe. But you also see a fair number of \n\t\t\t\t\t15626 text Theme / Example \n\t\t\t\t\t15627 text and \n\t\t\t\t\t15628 text Highlight Noteworthy\n\t\t\t\t\t15629 text  passages.\n\t\t\t\t\t15630 heading   , Value: 2\n\t\t\t\t15631 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15632 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct, \n\t\t\t\t\t15633 text to pass this Level.\n\t\t\t\t\t15634 text If it doesn\'t happen within 30 mins, that\'s fine. Feel free to keep working at it if you\'re so inclined, or to just come back to it at another time.\n\t\t\t\t\t15635 text Big Picture Reading Practice\n\t\t\t\t\t15636 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15637 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15638 text • See if there\'s any foreshadowing in that first paragraph, that\'s either setting up a  Position  (most studies have concluded, many people think), setting up a  Problem  (possibly asking a question like, "When did humans first start riding horses?), setting up a  Generalization  (something broad followed by  for example  or  a case in point ), or a  Debate  (proponents / opponents, some X\'s say / other X\'s say)\n\t\t\t\t\t15639 text As you read, keep testing yourself on retention by looking away from the screen and seeing if you can comfortably say the Main Ideas in your own words.\n\t\t\t\t\t15640 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15641 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15642 text • The question they\'re trying to answer is...\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15643 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15644 text • The reason we care about this book / this study / this person / this movement / this situation is because...\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15645 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15646 text • Side A of the debate believes... / Side B of the debate believes...\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15647 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15648 text • The Old idea was... / The New idea is...\n\t\t\t\t\t15649 text (Optional) Deluxe Learning Mode\n\t\t\t\t\t15650 text This takes longer, but makes a bigger difference on our brains. Use the NOTES panel (the page icon in the bottom left of the page pops open a NOTES panel you can move around) to record your thoughts. \n\t\t\t\t\t15651 text Big Picture Retention\n\t\t\t\t\t15652 text When you\'re done reading the passage, cover up the passage and type in your memory of the big ideas. If you\'re finding that you \n\t\t\t\t\t15653 text thought \n\t\t\t\t\t15654 text you understood what you were reading, but it\'s very hard to remember what to write down once you\'re not looking at the passage anymore, that means that you\'re not doing enough \n\t\t\t\t\t15655 text self-summarizing \n\t\t\t\t\t15656 text yet. When we read big ideas, we pause on those sentences long enough to digest them and simplify them in our own personal wording. This process is what leads to strong retention. We have an easier time remembering our own words than remembering an LSAT author\'s.\n\t\t\t\t\t15657 text Pre-phrasing\n\t\t\t\t\t15658 text When you\'re ready to start working through actual questions, use the NOTES panel to cover up the answer choices. Read a question stem, do whatever research you need to in the passage, and then type into the NOTES panel what you think the correct answer should say, or which sentence(s) will be the supporting text for the correct answer. If the question stem has no keywords, feel free to write nothing, or "no pre-phrase", or "beware strong language on first pass".\n\t\t\t\t\t15659 text Answer Evaluation \n\t\t\t\t\t15660 text Resize the NOTES panel so that you can see answers again, and when you pick your answer, type into the NOTES panel where your supporting text was found (you might need more than one sentence to support your answer, but usually it\'s just one sentence). Also type into the NOTES panel a specific reason why you\'re eliminating each answer choice. Don\'t just say "Out of Scope" without indicating which word or idea is out of scope. Don\'t just say "Too Strong" without typing which word or phrase was too strong. If everything in an answer is accurate, then list some other reason like Too Narrow for why it\'s wrong.\n\t\t\t\t15661 image Conditional Logic (Harder) Set 3\n\t\t\t\t15662 heading Conditional Logic (Harder) Set 3, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15663 text Conditional Logic (Harder) Set 3\n\t\t\t\t15664 text Pacing\n\t\t\t\t15665 text 37 mins\n\t\t\t\t15666 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15667 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15668 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15669 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15670 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15671 text Focus on finding \n\t\t\t\t\t15672 text Conditional Indicator\n\t\t\t\t\t15673 text  words and using them as a way to organize how you write or think about the If / Then rule. Write or think through the contrapositive as well. Beware the temptation to make illegal Backwards or Opposite moves.\n\t\t\t\t\t15674 text Conditional Logic intersects with different question types differently:\n\t\t\t\t\t15675 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15676 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15677 text • Principle  (the left side of the Principle matches the Evidence, the right side matches the Conclusion)\n\t\t\t\t\t15678 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15679 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15680 text • Parallel (diagramming these arguments with "algebraic recipes" allows us to be more picky and decisive when evaluating answers)\n\t\t\t\t\t15681 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15682 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15683 text • Assumption (the conclusion gives us an A --> Z logic path we want to prove, and the evidence + the correct answer choice assemble together to create that A --> Z path\xa0\xa0/ or the evidence gives us a conditional rule that is being used in drawing the conclusion, but we still need an answer choice to tell us something in order to clearly trigger that rule.)\n\t\t\t\t\t15684 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15685 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15686 text • Must Be True / Most Supported (multiple conditionals often chain together, and provided facts often match the contrapositive-trigger of a conditional and allow us to infer the contrapositive-outcome)\n\t\t\t\t\t15687 text \ufeff\n\t\t\t\t\t15688 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15689 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15690 text • Flaw / Parallel Flaw (Flaw + Conditional Logic usually means the  Necessary vs. Sufficient  flaw, which is using a rule in an illegal Backwards or Opposite fashion. Sometimes it involves messing up Or / And stuff)\n\t\t\t\t15691 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15692 text Try these 6 questions, \n\t\t\t\t\t15693 text level 5.\n\t\t\t\t\t15694 text Try them all within \n\t\t\t\t\t15695 text 11 minutes\n\t\t\t\t\t15696 text  (or 16, or 22), then circle back and confirm your thinking (untimed) before checking your previous answer and looking at the explanation.\n\t\t\t\t\t15697 text CONDITIONAL KEYWORDS\n\t\t\t\t\t15698 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15699 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15700 text • Put on  LEFT \n\t\t\t\t\t15701 text \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0if\n\t\t\t\t\t15702 text , when, any, each, all, every, the only, whenever, whoever, X\'s \n\t\t\t\t\t15703 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15704 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15705 text • Put it on the  RIGHT\n\t\t\t\t\t15706 text \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0only if\n\t\t\t\t\t15707 text , only, must, requires, ensures, will, always, implies, \n\t\t\t\t\t15708 text \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0presupposes, depends on, guarantees, \n\t\t\t\t\t15709 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15710 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15711 text • Put negated version of either idea on left ( IF-NOT )\n\t\t\t\t\t15712 text \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0unless\n\t\t\t\t\t15713 text , without, until except\n\t\t\t\t\t15714 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15715 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15716 text • NEGATIVE  to Positive conversions\n\t\t\t\t\t15717 text \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0No \n\t\t\t\t\t15718 text A\'s are B = All A\'s are ~B \n\t\t\t\t\t15719 text \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0Not all A\'s are B = Some A\'s are ~B\n\t\t\t\t\t15720 text \xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0\xa0Few A\'s are B = Most A\'s are ~B\n\t\t\t\t15721 image Parallel - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15722 heading Parallel - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15723 text Parallel - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15724 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15725 text 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15726 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15727 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15728 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15729 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15730 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15731 heading FINAL SHOWDOWN, Value: 1\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15732 text FINAL SHOWDOWN\n\t\t\t\t\t15733 heading 1\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15734 image\n\t\t\t\t\t15735 heading Level 5, Value: 1\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15736 text Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15737 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15738 text Get 4 of your last 5 correct\n\t\t\t\t\t15739 text ,  to clear this Level.\n\t\t\t\t15740 image Present Debate - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15741 heading Present Debate - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15742 text Present Debate - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15743 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15744 text 1 hr, 7 mins\n\t\t\t\t15745 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15746 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15747 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15748 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15749 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15750 text Synopsis\n\t\t\t\t\t15751 text Present a Debate is a common framework on Society and Law passages. After all, scholars in soft sciences (economics / anthropology / sociology, etc.) and legal scholars end up having to debate all the time because their subject matter is so frequently nuanced and many shades of gray.\xa0\n\t\t\t\t\t15752 text About 15% of passages are tagged with this framework. Usually the author inserts her opinion at the end of the passage, so these are commonly "Late-Thesis" type passages. Sometimes, though, the author stays out and just literally \n\t\t\t\t\t15753 text presents \n\t\t\t\t\t15754 text the debate without editorializing. \n\t\t\t\t\t15755 text Once you start to see 2 non-author points of view, think about what central question they\'re both addressing or answering. As you try to encode the main idea of each side of the debate, try to use \n\t\t\t\t\t15756 text Oppositional Pairings \n\t\t\t\t\t15757 text if possible.\n\t\t\t\t\t15758 text It\'s harder to remember, "Side A is in favor of more stringent COVID mitigation precautions" whereas "Side B thinks that the accompanying harms of remote learning and shuttered small businesses outweigh the health risks of staying open".\n\t\t\t\t\t15759 text It\'s easier to remember, "Side A is in favor of more lockdowns for a while, Side B opposes more lockdowns". So try to boil down each side\'s position into similar wording. Even if it\'s not binary "A vs. not-A" wording, we can make it fill in a common blank like, "Side A thinks the dinosaurs were killed by climate change, Side B says respiratory disease".\n\t\t\t\t15760 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15761 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct, \n\t\t\t\t\t15762 text to pass this Level.\n\t\t\t\t\t15763 text If it doesn\'t happen within 30 mins, that\'s fine. Feel free to keep working at it if you\'re so inclined, or to just come back to it at another time.\n\t\t\t\t\t15764 text As You\'re Reading ... \n\t\t\t\t\t15765 text \ufeffEarly Clues\n\t\t\t\t\t15766 text We see at least two points of view (POVs) that are not the author. We might see early attributions like, "Some critics say X. Others say Y", or perhaps we\'ll see mention of both Opponents and Proponents. Or there will be two schools of thought named (steady-state economists believe X, but neoclassical believe Y).\n\t\t\t\t\t15767 text Big Ideas to Track\n\t\t\t\t\t15768 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15769 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15770 text 1 . to consider diagramming the Conditional Logic are \ufeff\n\t\t\t\t\t15801 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15802 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15803 text • Must Be True\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15804 that could chain together. \n\t\t\t\t\t15824 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15825 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15826 text • On Flaw questions with conditional logic, look for authors to abuse conditional logic with illegal reversals or negations.\n\t\t\t\t15827 image Parallel Flaw - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15828 heading Parallel Flaw - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15829 text Parallel Flaw - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15830 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15837 heading The Final Showdown, Value: 1\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15838 text The Final Showdown\n\t\t\t\t\t15839 heading 1\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15840 image\n\t\t\t\t\t15841 heading Level 5, Value: 1\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15842 text Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15843 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15844 text Get 4 out of 5 correct,\n\t\t\t\t\t15845 text to pass this Level.\n\t\t\t\t15846 image Principle-Conform: Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15847 heading Principle-Conform: Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15848 text Principle-Conform: Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15849 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15850 text 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15851 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15852 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15853 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15854 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15855 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15856 text There are three varieties of \n\t\t\t\t\t15857 text Principle-Conform\n\t\t\t\t\t15858 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15859 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15860 text • The stimulus is a principle (or pair of principles)\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15861 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15862 text • The answers are principles\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15863 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15864 text • There are no explicit principles, just implied/illustrated ones\n\t\t\t\t\t15865 text Principles in Stimulus\n\t\t\t\t\t15866 text When the stimulus is providing an explicit principle (or two), we\'re usually being tested on our ability to apply a conditional rule. \n\t\t\t\t\t15867 text To find an answer that Conforms to this principle, we want an answer where the situation described matches the Trigger of the principle, and the judgment concluded matches the Outcome of the principle. (Even when the principles aren\'t expressed as conditionals, there will still usually be two things we need to make sure match up).\n\t\t\t\t\t15868 text Principles in Answers\n\t\t\t\t\t15869 text It\'s essentially the same mindset as a Principle-Strengthen question. We read the argument and then anticipate the principle underlying the argument by pre-phrasing "IF evidence, THEN conclusion". We expect the correct answer to \n\t\t\t\t\t15870 text Link \n\t\t\t\t\t15871 text language from the Evidence to the Conclusion\'s language.\xa0All that\'s different is that because the question stem says \n\t\t\t\t\t15872 text conform \n\t\t\t\t\t15873 text to the author\'s reasoning, we can\'t pick an answer that\'s overly strong. (That usually doesn\'t matter, but occasionally it does)\n\t\t\t\t\t15874 text Implicit Principles\n\t\t\t\t\t15875 text These feel similar to Parallel reasoning questions, because we\'re given an argument in the stimulus, and then each answer choice is its own argument on its own unique topic. We\'re looking for an underlying similarity to connect the correct answer to the original argument.\n\t\t\t\t\t15876 text On Parallel questions, those similarities come more in the form of technical / structural similarities (i.e. "Since the original argument had a \n\t\t\t\t\t15877 text Most \n\t\t\t\t\t15878 text premise and a \n\t\t\t\t\t15879 text Some \n\t\t\t\t\t15880 text premise, the correct answer\'s argument will also have those features").\n\t\t\t\t\t15881 text But with Principle-Conform it\'s more about the underlying gist or rule-of-thumb. We don\'t try to diagram the arguments. We just want to articulate a general moral to the story or operating principle that\'s guiding the author\'s thinking, and then we try to find an answer that matches that.\n\t\t\t\t15882 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15883 text Get 4 of your last 5 correct, \n\t\t\t\t\t15884 text untimed\n\t\t\t\t\t15885 text , to pass this \n\t\t\t\t\t15886 text level\n\t\t\t\t\t15887 text .\n\t\t\t\t15888 image Speed Drill - Level 2\n\t\t\t\t15889 heading Speed Drill - Level 2, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15890 text Speed Drill - Level 2\n\t\t\t\t15891 text Pacing\n\t\t\t\t15892 text 45 mins\n\t\t\t\t15893 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15894 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15895 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15896 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15897 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15898 text This is a trio of \n\t\t\t\t\t15899 text level 2\n\t\t\t\t\t15900 text  passages from tests 62, 64, 69. There\'s a \n\t\t\t\t\t15901 text Present Debate\n\t\t\t\t\t15902 text , an \n\t\t\t\t\t15903 text Old / New\n\t\t\t\t\t15904 text , and a \n\t\t\t\t\t15905 text Problem / Solution\n\t\t\t\t\t15906 text  passage, although you could probably see all three as Problem / Solution, if you prefer.\n\t\t\t\t\t15907 text The goal of this exercise is to practice a sustained, brisk "speedwalking" pace. When the test is offering us its easier items, we need to act like it.\n\t\t\t\t\t15908 text We need to try pushing our pace so that we can bank some extra time to spend on the hardest parts of a section.\n\t\t\t\t15909 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15910 text Set yourself an appropriate time limit.\n\t\t\t\t\t15911 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15912 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15913 text • If you aren\'t yet used to finishing all four passages with enough time, give yourself  27  mins for this threesome. \n\t\t\t\t\t15914 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15915 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15916 text • If you tend to get through all four, then try doing them in  22  mins. \n\t\t\t\t\t15917 text Either way, keep your eye on the clock and have a guess for all 21 Q\'s (even if it\'s a blind guess). \n\t\t\t\t\t15918 text The time limit is supposed to force us into experimenting with new behaviors:\n\t\t\t\t\t15919 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15920 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15921 text • when you have high confidence about an answer choice, pick it and move on without worrying about reading all the other answers you haven\'t seen yet. (high confidence comes when we find an answer choice that matches the  meaning  of a line in the passage, but an exact  language  match usually means a trap answer. but  doesn\'t  match up with language in the passage, but we can tell LSAT has put some work into disguising it with synonyms or different syntax. \n\t\t\t\t\t15922 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15923 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15924 text • if you get four or five words into an answer choice and already see something you don\'t like, get out of there. we need to conserve time and mental energy by not processing the full sentence of every answer choice. find  earlier  reasons to disqualify an answer.\n\t\t\t\t\t15925 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15926 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15927 text • get the passage read in 2.5 minutes or less. be content to simply determine the topic and framework, find the ideas that fill your framework boxes, and don\'t worry about grabbing too much else. Read the first paragraph carefully, and read the 1st sentence of other paragraphs carefully, and read any  pivot  sentences ( but, yet, however ) carefully. Let the rest of it breeze by.\n\t\t\t\t\t15928 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15929 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15930 text • skip the worst problem in each passage set. we will tend to overspend time on that even though we have a lower average accuracy on that problem, so it\'s a bad value.\n\t\t\t\t\t15931 text Hit SUBMIT SET when the timer runs out. Then take a 2nd untimed look at the questions and explanations.\n\t\t\t\t15932 image Role - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15933 heading Role - Level 5, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15934 text Role - Level 5\n\t\t\t\t15935 text Level Drill\n\t\t\t\t15936 text 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15937 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15938 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15939 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15940 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15941 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15942 text On harder \n\t\t\t\t\t15943 text Role \n\t\t\t\t\t15944 text questions, we\'re likely to see a couple patterns emerge:\n\t\t\t\t\t15945 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15946 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15947 text • Intermediate Conclusion?  Many of the harder problems test the existence of an Intermediate Conclusion, even if the claim we\'re being asked about isn\'t itself that. Answer choices describing a Premise might differ by saying, "It\'s provides direct support for the Conclusion" vs. "It provide support for a claim that then provides direct support for the Conclusion".\n\t\t\t\t\t15948 text To assess whether a claim is or isn\'t an Intermediate Conclusion, we want to ask ourselves, "\n\t\t\t\t\t15949 text Is there\n\t\t\t\t\t15950 text Support\n\t\t\t\t\t15951 text  for this claim? Why should we believe this claim? Does anything else in the paragraph sound like it\'s answering that question?"\n\t\t\t\t\t15952 text Often, when there \n\t\t\t\t\t15953 text isn\'t \n\t\t\t\t\t15954 text a supporting idea present and thus the claim you\'re examining is really just a Premise, it\'s useful to think about how \n\t\t\t\t\t15955 text you\n\t\t\t\t\t15956 text would support that claim.\n\t\t\t\t\t15957 text If you\'re asking yourself, "Was the claim \n\t\t\t\t\t15958 text You shouldn\'t tell jokes at a funeral \n\t\t\t\t\t15959 text supported?" Supply your own answer, just get your brain hearing what actual support would sound like:\xa0\xa0"you shouldn\'t tell jokes at a funeral \n\t\t\t\t\t15960 text because\n\t\t\t\t\t15961 text ... funerals are a somber occasion and telling jokes makes it seem like you\'re not respecting the gravity of the situation". By articulating what support would sound like, you can sometimes help strengthen your conviction that no support was provided, if you\'re not seeing any claims like that.\n\t\t\t\t\t15962 content list\n\t\t\t\t\t\t15963 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t15964 text • Relational language, rather than classic Argument Role language.  Harder problems tend to supply fewer answers with recognizable terms like "Premise, Conclusion, Intermediate Conclusion" and either use more complicated abstract phrases to signify the same idea, or they don\'t really concern themselves with those labels at all. Instead, they just conversationally describe how the claims relate to each other, almost more like a  Method  of reasoning question. \n\t\t\t\t15965 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15966 text Get 4 out of your last 5 correct,\n\t\t\t\t\t15967 text to pass this level.\n\t\t\t\t15968 image Speedwalking LR (set 2)\n\t\t\t\t15969 heading Speedwalking LR (set 2), Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15970 text Speedwalking LR (set 2)\n\t\t\t\t15971 text Pacing\n\t\t\t\t15972 text 45 mins\n\t\t\t\t15973 button Info\n\t\t\t\t\t15974 text Info\n\t\t\t\t15975 link Description: Start, Value: …\n\t\t\t\t15976 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t15977 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15978 text LENGTH\n\t\t\t\t\t15979 text  -- 15 Q\'s, 15 minutes (1.5x = 22, 2x = 30)\n\t\t\t\t\t15980 text TYPES\n\t\t\t\t\t15981 text  -- Paradox, Flaw, Role, Main Conclusion, Necessary Assumption, Sufficient Assumption, Strengthen, Weaken, Method, and Must Be True.\n\t\t\t\t\t15982 text LEVEL\n\t\t\t\t\t15983 text  -- 1\n\t\t\t\t\t15984 text Wait a sec -- these are all level 1? I thought this activity was listed as level 5?\n\t\t\t\t\t15985 text Yes, because the goal is something a level 5 student needs to work on:\xa0\xa0be able to quickly take care of easier questions, so that you\'ll have more time and brainpower in reserves for the harder, more flexible thinking questions in the section.\n\t\t\t\t\t15986 text Given how many subtle reading traps there are on LSAT, it\'s sometimes difficult to ever let yourself believe that an answer you find appealing is correct. "It\'s never this easy", we might think. But, sure it is! Sometimes it really is that easy. We need to improve our ability to \n\t\t\t\t\t15987 text let the easy be easy\n\t\t\t\t\t15988 text .\n\t\t\t\t\t15989 text And we need to develop enough self-trust while we\'re doing easier problems that we can pick up our pace when possible.\n\t\t\t\t15990 container\n\t\t\t\t\t15991 text Try to get through these 15 questions in 15 mins. Keep yourself going at a brisk pace. When you have a strong idea of what you\'re looking for (like on Main Conclusion, Role, Sufficient Assumption, Flaw), try to be proactive about scanning for and finding your answer, rather than reading all five choices start to finish.\n\t\t\t\t\t15992 text However, on tasks where we compare the impact of new information (like Paradox, Strengthen, Weaken), we may still need to use more time to consider all five answers.\n\t\t\t\t\t15993 text If your thinking feels unfinished on any of them, flag them as you go (so that you can maintain your brisk pace), and then take a second look at them after the timer goes off before you check your answer / the explanation.\n\t\t\t\t15994 image PrepTest 141 - Section 3\n\t\t\t\t15995 heading PrepTest 141 - Section 3, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t15996 text PrepTest 141 - Section 3\n\t\t\t\t15997 text Timed Section 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t15998 button Take Section\n\t\t\t\t\t15999 text Take Section\n\t\t\t\t16000 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t16001 image PrepTest 143 - Section 1\n\t\t\t\t16002 heading PrepTest 143 - Section 1, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t16003 text PrepTest 143 - Section 1\n\t\t\t\t16004 text Timed Section 1 hr, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t16005 button Take Section\n\t\t\t\t\t16006 text Take Section\n\t\t\t\t16007 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t16008 image PrepTest 156\n\t\t\t\t16009 heading PrepTest 156, Value: 6\n\t\t\t\t\t16010 text PrepTest 156\n\t\t\t\t16011 text Practice Test 4 hrs, 30 mins\n\t\t\t\t16012 button Take Test\n\t\t\t\t\t16013 text Take Test\n\t\t\t\t16014 text \uf34c\n\t\t\t\t16015 button \uf2c2\n\t\t\t\t\t16016 text \uf2c2\n\t\t\t16017 container\n\t\t\t\t16018 heading Week 15, Value: 3\n\t\t\t\t\t16019 container\n\t\t\t\t\t\t16020 text Week  15\n\t\t\t\t16021 text January 3rd - 9th, 2027\n\t\t\t\t16022 text Est.
